title: Backlight helper applies brightness on the wrong device scale when spawned while the panel connector is disabled (hybrid GPU, two backlight devices)
line: On hybrid-GPU laptops with two backlight devices, the screen no longer comes back about 5x too bright after it turns off on idle.
explanation: The backlight helper is started fresh for each request and picks its reference device from /sys/class/backlight, preferring raw devices whose connector says enabled. When the screen wakes up the panel's connector is still disabled, so it fell back to all raw devices in reverse name order, put nvidia_0 (max 100) first, and rescaled the value powerdevil sent on intel_backlight's 0..496 scale against 100: 4% became 104/496. Now, when no connector is enabled, the helper keeps using the devices that belong to a connector before falling back to all raw devices, so it picks the same device as when the screen is on.

commits.message:
backlighthelper: keep the panel's device while its connector is disabled

Brightness set as the screen woke up found the panel's connector still
disabled, so the helper took another GPU's raw backlight as reference
and rescaled the value. Keep using the devices of a connector then.

BUG: 523341

media.caption: Master's helper on a fake hybrid-GPU sysfs: with the eDP connector off it takes nvidia_0 (max 100) as reference and writes 104/496 to intel_backlight for 4% brightness (the reporter's exact numbers)
Fixed helper, same steps: with the connector off it keeps intel_backlight as reference and writes 21/496, the same as with the connector on

review.text: The diagnosis in BacklightHelper::getBacklightTypeDevices() is spot-on: preferring the DRM-connector backlight while its connector is temporarily disabled during wake-from-idle prevents the helper from flipping to nvidia_0 (max 100) and rescaling intel_backlight ~5x too bright. However, grouping every raw device that merely has a device/enabled file into rawConnector ahead of rawAll will regress hybrid-GPU laptops whose panel is muxed to the dGPU (nvidia_0, no device/enabled) while the iGPU still exposes a disconnected eDP connector (intel_backlight with device/enabled=disabled and device/status=disconnected), completely dropping nvidia_0. Checking device/status so disconnected connectors do not shadow rawAll avoids that regression while keeping the fix minimal.
changes: In BacklightHelper::getBacklightTypeDevices(), check <device>/device/status alongside <device>/device/enabled and only add a disabled-connector raw device to rawConnector when its connector status is not "disconnected" (e.g. "connected" or status file absent), so an unused/muxed-away DRM connector cannot hide an active non-connector backlight like nvidia_0.
